theory.intro: A polygon is regular if all its sides are equal AND all its angles are equal. If either varies, it is irregular.
facts: **Regular**: all sides equal and all angles equal (e.g. square, equilateral triangle).
**Irregular**: at least one side or angle is different.
Equal sides are shown by tick marks; equal angles are often shown by matching arc marks.
steps: Check whether all sides are equal (look at the tick marks or lengths).
Check whether all angles are equal.
If both are equal it is regular; otherwise it is irregular.

foundation.solution_text:
All three sides are equal and all three angles are equal.
The triangle is regular.

All four sides are equal and all four angles are equal.
The square is regular.

The sides are all equal, but the angles are not all equal.
The rhombus is irregular.

The angles are all equal, but the side lengths are not all equal.
The rectangle is irregular.

At least one side length differs from the others.
The pentagon is irregular.

A regular polygon needs equal sides **and** equal angles.
Because the angles differ, the hexagon is irregular.

development.solution_text:
All six sides are equal and all six angles are equal.
The hexagon is regular.

development.question_text: An octagon has eight equal angles, but two of its sides are longer than the other six. Classify it.
development.solution_text:
Equal angles satisfy only one part of the definition.
Because the eight sides are not all equal, the octagon is irregular.

development.question_text: A pentagon has five equal side lengths. What extra information is needed before you can call it regular?
development.solution_text: Its five interior angles must also all be equal.

Noah has checked only the side condition.
He must also check whether all four angles are equal before deciding whether the quadrilateral is regular.

development.question_text: A quadrilateral has four angles of $90^{\circ}$ and four sides of $5$ cm. Is it regular? Give both checks.
development.solution_text:
All four angles are equal because each is $90^{\circ}$.
All four sides are equal because each is $5$ cm.
The quadrilateral is regular.

development.question_text: A triangle has side lengths $8$ cm, $8$ cm and $5$ cm. Its angles are $71^{\circ}$, $71^{\circ}$ and $38^{\circ}$. Classify it as regular or irregular.
development.solution_text:
The three sides are not all equal, and the three angles are not all equal.
The triangle is irregular.

mastery.question_text: A polygon has all its sides equal. Priya says this proves it is regular. Decide whether her claim is always true and justify your answer.
mastery.solution_text:
The claim is not always true.
A non-square rhombus has all sides equal but has two different angle sizes, so it is irregular.

mastery.question_text: A polygon has all its angles equal. Ben says this proves it is regular. Give a quadrilateral counterexample and explain.
mastery.solution_text:
A non-square rectangle has four equal right angles but has two long sides and two short sides.
Its sides are not all equal, so it is irregular.

mastery.question_text: A regular pentagon is stretched sideways so that some sides and angles change. It still has five sides. Is the new pentagon regular? Explain.
mastery.solution_text:
The number of sides does not decide regularity.
After the stretch, the sides and angles are no longer all equal, so the new pentagon is irregular.
